name: Matthew

overview.author: Matthew (also called Levi), a tax collector who became one of the twelve apostles (9:9; 10:3). Early church tradition unanimously attributes the Gospel to him.
overview.date: Probably written in the AD 50s or 60s, before the destruction of the temple in AD 70.
overview.audience: Primarily Jewish Christians, though with a clear mission to all nations.
overview.setting: Jesus’ life, ministry, death, and resurrection in Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem, about 4 BC to AD 30/33.
overview.purpose: To show that Jesus is the promised Messiah, fulfilling the Scriptures, who brings the kingdom of heaven, teaches with authority, and sends His disciples to make disciples of all nations.
overview.structure: Narrative sections alternate with five major teaching blocks: the Sermon on the Mount (5–7), the mission discourse (10), the kingdom parables (13), community life (18), and the end times (24–25), framed by Jesus’ birth (1–2) and His passion and resurrection (26–28).

themes.title: Fulfillment
themes.text: Matthew repeatedly says “this was to fulfill what the Lord had spoken by the prophet.”

themes.title: Jesus the King
themes.text: Jesus is the Son of David and the King of the Jews.

themes.title: The Kingdom of Heaven
themes.text: Jesus announces and embodies God’s reign.

themes.title: Righteousness
themes.text: Jesus calls for a righteousness that exceeds the Pharisees’, from the heart.

themes.title: Discipleship
themes.text: Following Jesus means obedience, sacrifice, and fruitfulness.

themes.title: God With Us
themes.text: Jesus is Immanuel (1:23) and promises “I am with you always” (28:20).

themes.title: Mission to All Nations
themes.text: From the magi to the Great Commission, the gospel goes to the Gentiles.

christInBook.text: Jesus is the son of David and the son of Abraham, the heir of God’s promises.
Jesus is Immanuel, God with us.
Jesus came not to abolish the Law and the Prophets but to fulfill them.
Peter confesses Jesus as Christ, and Jesus foretells His death and resurrection.
The Son of Man came to give His life as a ransom for many.
All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to the risen Jesus.

crossReferences.note: The Son of Man with all authority.

reflection: Which part of the Sermon on the Mount most challenges how you live?
Jesus says, “Come to me... and I will give you rest.” Where do you need His rest?
How would you answer Jesus’ question “Who do you say that I am?” (16:15)?
What parable best describes your own response to God’s word?
Who is one person you can help become a disciple of Jesus?

chapterList.title: The Genealogy and Birth of Jesus
chapterList.summary: Matthew traces Jesus’ genealogy from Abraham through David and the exile to Joseph, including surprising women like Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and Bathsheba. Mary is found to be with child from the Holy Spirit. An angel tells Joseph to name Him Jesus, “for he will save his people from their sins,” fulfilling Isaiah’s Immanuel prophecy.
questions: Why does Matthew begin with a genealogy?
What does the inclusion of these women tell you about God’s grace?
What do the names “Jesus” and “Immanuel” reveal about Him?

chapterList.title: The Magi and the Flight to Egypt
chapterList.summary: Wise men from the east follow a star to worship the newborn King of the Jews. Herod, troubled, plots to kill Him. The magi worship Jesus with gifts. Warned in a dream, Joseph flees with Mary and Jesus to Egypt. Herod massacres Bethlehem’s boys. After Herod dies, the family settles in Nazareth.
questions: How do the magi and Herod respond differently to Jesus?
How does “Out of Egypt I called my son” connect Jesus to Israel (Hosea 11:1)?
What does Joseph’s obedience teach you?

chapterList.title: John the Baptist and Jesus’ Baptism
chapterList.summary: John preaches in the wilderness: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” He calls for fruit in keeping with repentance and promises one who will baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire. Jesus is baptized; the Spirit descends like a dove, and the Father says, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”
questions: What does it mean to bear fruit in keeping with repentance (3:8)?
Why was Jesus baptized (3:15)?
How is the Trinity revealed at Jesus’ baptism?

chapterList.title: The Temptation and First Disciples
chapterList.summary: The Spirit leads Jesus into the wilderness, where He fasts 40 days. He answers each of Satan’s temptations with Scripture: “Man shall not live by bread alone.” Jesus begins preaching in Galilee, calls Peter, Andrew, James, and John to follow Him and become fishers of men, and heals many.
questions: How did Jesus defeat temptation?
How is Jesus the faithful Son where Israel failed in the wilderness?
What did the first disciples leave to follow Jesus?

chapterList.title: The Beatitudes and the Law Fulfilled
chapterList.summary: On a mountain Jesus teaches: “Blessed are the poor in spirit... those who mourn... the meek... those who hunger and thirst for righteousness.” His disciples are salt and light. He came to fulfill the Law. He deepens its commands: anger, lust, oaths, retaliation, and loving enemies. “You therefore must be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.”
questions: Which Beatitude speaks most to you right now?
How are believers salt and light (5:13–16)?
How does Jesus go beyond outward obedience to the heart?

chapterList.title: Prayer, Treasure, and Worry
chapterList.summary: Jesus warns against practicing righteousness to be seen by others in giving, prayer, and fasting. He teaches the Lord’s Prayer. Lay up treasures in heaven, for where your treasure is, your heart will be. You cannot serve God and money. Do not be anxious; “seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness.”
questions: Why does motive matter in religious practice?
What do the requests in the Lord’s Prayer teach about priorities?
How does Jesus help you deal with anxiety (6:25–34)?

chapterList.title: The Narrow Gate and the Wise Builder
chapterList.summary: Jesus warns against judging hypocritically. Ask, seek, and knock, for the Father gives good gifts. Treat others as you want to be treated. Enter by the narrow gate. Beware of false prophets known by their fruit. The one who hears and does Jesus’ words is like a man who builds his house on the rock.
questions: How do you take the log out of your own eye (7:3–5)?
What do 7:21–23 teach about true faith?
What does building on the rock look like in your life?

chapterList.title: Authority Over Disease and Storm
chapterList.summary: Jesus heals a leper, a centurion’s servant (marveling at the Gentile’s faith), and Peter’s mother-in-law. He calls would-be followers to count the cost. He calms a storm: “What sort of man is this, that even winds and sea obey him?” He casts demons into pigs.
questions: What did the centurion understand about Jesus’ authority?
What does 8:19–22 teach about following Jesus?
How does Jesus’ calming of the storm reveal who He is?

chapterList.title: Forgiveness, Healing, and the Call of Matthew
chapterList.summary: Jesus forgives and heals a paralytic. He calls Matthew the tax collector and eats with sinners: “I desire mercy, and not sacrifice.” He raises a girl, heals a bleeding woman, two blind men, and a mute man. Seeing the crowds like sheep without a shepherd, He says, “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few.”
questions: Why did Jesus forgive the paralytic before healing him?
How does Jesus’ table fellowship with sinners challenge you?
Who could you pray for to become a laborer in the harvest (9:38)?

chapterList.title: The Twelve Sent Out
chapterList.summary: Jesus sends the twelve apostles to the lost sheep of Israel, with authority to heal and proclaim the kingdom. He warns of persecution: “I am sending you out as sheep in the midst of wolves.” Do not fear those who kill the body. Whoever loses his life for Jesus’ sake will find it.
questions: How did Jesus prepare His disciples for opposition?
Why should we not fear people (10:28–31)?
What does it mean to take up your cross (10:38–39)?

chapterList.title: Come to Me
chapterList.summary: John the Baptist asks from prison whether Jesus is the one. Jesus points to His works. He praises John and rebukes cities that did not repent. He thanks the Father for revealing truth to little children. “Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest... my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
questions: How did Jesus answer John’s doubt?
Why were Chorazin and Bethsaida judged (11:20–24)?
What is Jesus’ yoke, and how does it give rest?

chapterList.title: Lord of the Sabbath
chapterList.summary: Jesus defends His disciples for picking grain on the Sabbath; He is lord of the Sabbath. He heals on the Sabbath, and the Pharisees plot to destroy Him. He is the servant of Isaiah 42. Accused of casting out demons by Beelzebul, He warns of blasphemy against the Spirit. He gives the sign of Jonah. His family are those who do the Father’s will.
questions: What does it mean that Jesus is lord of the Sabbath?
Why is attributing the Spirit’s work to Satan so serious?
What is the sign of Jonah (12:39–41)?

chapterList.title: Parables of the Kingdom
chapterList.summary: Jesus teaches in parables: the sower and soils, the weeds among wheat, the mustard seed, the leaven, the hidden treasure, the pearl of great price, and the net. He explains why He speaks in parables. He is rejected in His hometown of Nazareth.
questions: Which soil best describes your heart now?
What do the mustard seed and leaven teach about the kingdom?
What would you give up for the treasure of the kingdom (13:44–46)?

chapterList.title: Feeding Five Thousand and Walking on Water
chapterList.summary: Herod beheads John the Baptist. Jesus feeds five thousand men with five loaves and two fish. He walks on the water; Peter walks toward Him, sinks when he sees the wind, and Jesus catches him. The disciples worship: “Truly you are the Son of God.”
questions: What does the feeding of the five thousand reveal about Jesus?
Why did Peter begin to sink (14:30)?
What storms in your life call you to keep your eyes on Jesus?

chapterList.title: Tradition and Faith
chapterList.summary: Jesus rebukes the Pharisees for breaking God’s commands for their traditions; what defiles comes from the heart. A Canaanite woman persistently asks for her daughter’s healing, and Jesus praises her great faith. He heals many and feeds four thousand.
questions: How can tradition replace God’s word (15:6)?
What defiles a person (15:18–20)?
What made the Canaanite woman’s faith great?

chapterList.title: You Are the Christ
chapterList.summary: The Pharisees and Sadducees demand a sign. Jesus warns of their leaven. Peter confesses, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Jesus will build His church. He foretells His death and resurrection, rebukes Peter, and calls disciples to deny themselves and take up their cross.
questions: Who do you say Jesus is (16:15–16)?
Why did Jesus rebuke Peter so strongly (16:23)?
What does it mean to lose your life to find it?

chapterList.title: The Transfiguration
chapterList.summary: On a mountain, Jesus is transfigured, His face shining like the sun. Moses and Elijah appear, and the Father says, “This is my beloved Son... listen to him.” Jesus heals a boy the disciples could not heal: faith like a mustard seed can move mountains. He again predicts His death and pays the temple tax.
questions: What does the transfiguration reveal about Jesus?
What does “listen to him” mean for your life?
Why couldn’t the disciples heal the boy (17:19–20)?

chapterList.title: Greatness and Forgiveness
chapterList.summary: The greatest in the kingdom is one who humbles himself like a child. Jesus warns against causing little ones to sin and tells of the shepherd seeking one lost sheep. He teaches how to address sin in the church. Peter asks how often to forgive; Jesus says seventy-seven times, and tells of the unforgiving servant.
questions: What does childlike humility look like?
What steps does Jesus give for confronting sin (18:15–17)?
Why must forgiven people forgive (18:32–35)?

chapterList.title: Marriage, Children, and Riches
chapterList.summary: Jesus teaches on marriage and divorce, citing creation. He blesses little children. A rich young man asks what good deed to do for eternal life but goes away sorrowful. “With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.” The first will be last.
questions: What does Jesus teach about God’s design for marriage (19:4–6)?
Why was it hard for the rich young man to follow Jesus?
What have you left to follow Jesus, and what does He promise (19:29)?

chapterList.title: Laborers and the Ransom
chapterList.summary: In the parable of the vineyard workers, all receive the same wage by the master’s generosity. Jesus predicts His death a third time. James and John’s mother asks for places of honor; Jesus says the greatest must be a servant, “even as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.” He heals two blind men.
questions: What does the parable of the workers teach about grace?
How does Jesus redefine greatness?
What does it mean that Jesus gave His life as a ransom (20:28)?

chapterList.title: The Triumphal Entry
chapterList.summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem on a donkey to cries of “Hosanna to the Son of David!” He cleanses the temple: “My house shall be called a house of prayer.” He curses a fruitless fig tree. His authority is questioned. Parables of two sons and wicked tenants expose the leaders’ rejection.
questions: How does the entry fulfill Zechariah 9:9?
Why did Jesus cleanse the temple?
What is the stone the builders rejected (21:42)?

chapterList.title: Questions in the Temple
chapterList.summary: Jesus tells the parable of the wedding feast. Leaders try to trap Him: on taxes (“Render to Caesar”), resurrection, and the greatest commandment: love God with all your heart and your neighbor as yourself. Jesus asks how David can call the Messiah “Lord.”
questions: Who are those invited to the wedding feast?
What does “render to God the things that are God’s” mean for you?
How do the two great commandments summarize the law?

chapterList.title: Woes to the Pharisees
chapterList.summary: Jesus warns against the scribes and Pharisees who do not practice what they preach and love honor. He pronounces seven woes on their hypocrisy: shutting the kingdom, neglecting justice, mercy, and faithfulness, cleaning the outside of the cup. He laments over Jerusalem like a hen gathering her chicks.
questions: How do the Pharisees’ faults appear in religious people today?
What are the “weightier matters of the law” (23:23)?
What does Jesus’ lament reveal about His heart?

chapterList.title: Signs of the End
chapterList.summary: Jesus predicts the temple’s destruction. He warns of false christs, wars, famines, persecution, and the abomination of desolation. The gospel will be proclaimed to all nations. The Son of Man will come on the clouds with power. No one knows the day or hour, so stay awake.
questions: What warnings does Jesus give about deception?
How does 24:14 motivate mission?
How can you be ready for Jesus’ return?

chapterList.title: Ten Virgins, Talents, and the Final Judgment
chapterList.summary: Jesus tells of ten virgins, five ready and five foolish. He tells of servants given talents, rewarded for faithfulness. At the final judgment, the Son of Man separates sheep from goats: “As you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.”
questions: What does it mean to be ready like the wise virgins?
What “talents” has God given you to invest?
How does 25:40 shape how you treat people in need?

chapterList.title: The Last Supper and Gethsemane
chapterList.summary: The leaders plot to kill Jesus. A woman anoints Him at Bethany. Judas agrees to betray Him for thirty pieces of silver. At the Passover, Jesus institutes the Lord’s Supper: “This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.” In Gethsemane He prays, “Not as I will, but as you will.” He is arrested; Peter denies Him three times.
questions: What does the Lord’s Supper mean (26:26–29)?
What does Jesus’ prayer in Gethsemane teach about surrender?
How do Peter’s denials and Judas’s betrayal differ?

chapterList.title: The Crucifixion
chapterList.summary: Judas, remorseful, hangs himself. Pilate offers to release Jesus or Barabbas; the crowd chooses Barabbas. Jesus is mocked, crucified between two robbers, and cries, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” The temple curtain tears, and a centurion says, “Truly this was the Son of God!” Jesus is buried in Joseph’s tomb, which is sealed and guarded.
questions: What does the Barabbas exchange picture about substitution?
Why did Jesus cry out Psalm 22:1?
What does the torn curtain mean (27:51; Hebrews 10:19–20)?

chapterList.title: He Is Risen
chapterList.summary: At dawn on the first day, women find the stone rolled away. An angel says, “He is not here, for he has risen, as he said.” Jesus meets them. The guards are bribed to spread a lie. In Galilee, Jesus declares all authority is His and commissions: “Go therefore and make disciples of all nations... I am with you always, to the end of the age.”
questions: Why is the resurrection central to the faith?
What are the parts of the Great Commission (28:19–20)?
How does “I am with you always” encourage your obedience?

tagline: Jesus the Messiah, Son of David, King of the kingdom of heaven
readingPlan: 28 chapters: one chapter a day takes 28 days; two a day takes about 14 days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
